statements.statement: The tool uses new URL() / WHATWG URL parsing; :443 is dropped as the default port (80 http/ws, 443 https/wss, 21 ftp) while the request still uses 443; port placeholder; RFC 3986 Appendix B host comparison.
statements.qualification: Added: the fragment is not sent to the server, and fetch() rejects a URL that carries credentials. Ports: SPECIAL 587, defaultPort 1039, placeholder 1200. RFC check 657-672, 1053-1059.

statements.statement: Without a scheme new URL() throws; the tool explains and suggests https://; relative links need a base URL; localhost:3000/api parses as scheme localhost: with no host.
statements.qualification: diagnoseFailure 934-968; schemeLooksLikeHost 1030-1032.

statements.statement: Query decoded with application/x-www-form-urlencoded: + is a space; %2B is a literal plus.
statements.qualification: parseQuery 849-868; URLSearchParams comparison in test-url-parser.

statements.statement: Percent-escapes that are not UTF-8 decode to U+FFFD; the tool shows that and keeps the raw bytes.
statements.qualification: Rewritten: URLSearchParams and this tool percent-decode as UTF-8; the browser still sends the original bytes, so a legacy-charset server can read them. URL Standard 5.1; URLSearchParams check: caf%E9 -> caf�.

statements.statement: Untouched pairs keep their exact text; only the edited pair is URLSearchParams-encoded (space as +).
statements.qualification: serializeQuery 872-881; per-pair raw 862; test compares 3,000 random queries.

statements.statement: No request with the URL and no storage; analytics records only tool name and action parse on commit/example/suggestion, deduplicated; URL excluded; password masked.
statements.qualification: Component has no fetch/storage/ztPersist (test assertion). persistence.ts and network.ts have no url-parser entry. trackTool only tool_name/tool_action (BaseLayout 207-212); render(true) at 1383-1386, 1206-1211, 1373-1381, 1421-1427; dedupe 1367-1370.

statements.statement: The WHATWG parser trims leading/trailing spaces, removes tabs/newlines, and percent-encodes some characters; for special schemes it lowercases the host, punycodes IDNs, resolves dot segments and drops default ports; a non-special scheme keeps an opaque host.
statements.qualification: strips spaces -> trims leading and trailing spaces (stripInput 599-603; URL Standard first two steps). Host lowercasing, Punycode, dot segments and default ports scoped to special schemes: Node 24 keeps foo://EXAMPLE.com/ as EXAMPLE.com and percent-encodes a non-ASCII opaque host.

statements.statement: The example normalizes to /a/c, drops :443 and reports %zz at position 63; RFC 3986 3.2.1 masks the password.
statements.qualification: up-check recomputed by test; codepoint position 63 verified from the source text; note code at 1015-1018 and 1039, 1061-1062.

statements.statement: The + is decoded as a space because query strings follow application/x-www-form-urlencoded, the same rules as URLSearchParams.
statements.qualification: Rewritten: the tool reads the query with the application/x-www-form-urlencoded parser, the same one URLSearchParams uses. The URL Standard does not define all query strings as form-urlencoded.

statements.statement: Rebuilding with URLSearchParams.toString() re-encodes every pair, so the URL changes even when nothing is edited; this tool preserves untouched pairs.
statements.qualification: Changed to "can change": canonical pairs round-trip unchanged. Examples flag -> flag=, %zz -> %25zz and %E4%B8 -> %EF%BF%BD verified with URLSearchParams.
